 3.6M ladders recalled nationwide following serious injuries 
 Zach Kaplan 
 Updated: Nov 6, 2026 / 01:18 PM CST 
 Comments: 
 NOW PLAYING
 ( NewsNation ) — A Utah company is recalling more than 3.6 million ladders following numerous injury reports, federal regulators announced this week.
 The recall applies to 11 models of Little Giant ladders with Rapid Locks, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission . They were sold at Lowe’s, Costco, and other stores nationwide from December 2015 to October 2026 for between $100 and $1,000. They were also sold online at Lowes.com, Amazon.com, Costco.com, LittleGiantLadders.com and other websites. 
 Why were more than 3.6M ladders recalled? 
 The recall follows “25 reports of the ladders retracting, including 19 reports of injuries, consisting of three reports of head injuries such as traumatic brain injury, skull fracture, concussion, vision loss, hearing loss and cognitive impairment,” the CPSC said. 
 Kale chips recalled nationwide over potential metal contamination 
 There were an additional 16 reports of injuries, including joint or bone fractures, lacerations, and bruising, the CPSC added. Little Giant has also received 39 reports of the Rapid Lock system malfunctioning. 
 “The ladders can suddenly retract if the Rapid Locks are not fully engaged, posing a fall hazard to consumers,” the CPSC warned. 
 Which Little Giant ladders with Rapid Locks models were recalled? 
 Consumers are advised to stop using the ladder until they review the information on Little Giant’s website and contact the company for a repair kit with warning labels and instructions. 
 GM recalls more than 67K vehicles over brake failure fears 
 The recalled models specifically include the Adjustable Fortress 2.0, Conquest 2.0, Dark Horse 2.0, Epic, King Kombo XT, Leveler, MegaLite, MegaLite+, Multi, Quantum and Vector. They all have the brand name “Little Giant” and model number written on the side.
